t: This is St Augustine's, a Grade II star listed Anglican church on Queen's Gate in Brompton. It was built in 1865 and designed by William Butterfield. Butterfield was a British Gothic Revival architect, associated with the Oxford Movement, and he is noted for his use of polychromy, meaning patterns made with bricks and stone of different colours. So when you look at the walls and the way the materials are used, you are seeing the hand of an architect with a very distinctive style.
